turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: That's an interesting question. While the McGurk effect primarily affects words with conflicting auditory and visual information, research does suggest that people may have more difficulty processing words with multiple syllables, especially in noisy environments or when the audio quality is poor. This is related to the concept of cognitive load and the way our brains process linguistic information.
